Ontario's employment rate was higher than Quebec's in September 2026, by 0.2 percentage points.

| Province | Employment rate | Vector |
|---|---|---|
| Ontario | 60.1% | v2063951 |
| Quebec | 59.9% | v2063762 |

Both figures are seasonally adjusted rates for people aged 15 and over, both genders combined, for September 2026. The source is Statistics Canada Labour Force Survey, table 14-10-0287-01.

The gap is small, so it may be within the survey's sampling error. I didn't check the standard errors.

Canada's youth unemployment rate (ages 15 to 24, both genders, seasonally adjusted) was:

- **September 2026:** 13.0%
- **September 2025:** 14.6%

That is a drop of 1.6 percentage points over the year.

Source: Statistics Canada, Table 14-10-0287-01 (Labour force characteristics, monthly, seasonally adjusted), vector v2062842. Source page: https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=1410028701

Canada lost about 68,300 jobs in September 2026 (seasonally adjusted), a decline of about 0.3%.

- **August 2026:** 21,173.1 thousand employed
- **September 2026:** 21,104.8 thousand employed
- **Change:** −68.3 thousand

This is my own subtraction of the two published monthly levels, not a change figure Statistics Canada published. The estimates carry sampling error, so the change may not be statistically significant. I didn't pull the standard error of the month-to-month change, so I can't say either way.

**Source:** Statistics Canada, Labour Force Survey, table 14-10-0287-01 (employment, both sexes, 15 years and over, seasonally adjusted), vector v2062811, reference periods August and September 2026. https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=1410028701

The average hourly wage of employees in Canada in September 2026 was **$37.64**. That is up **$0.86 (about 2.3%)** from $36.78 in September 2025.

- **Source:** Statistics Canada, Table 14-10-0063-01, "Employee wages by industry, monthly, unadjusted for seasonality", vector v2132579.
- **Scope:** Average hourly wage rate, all employees (full- and part-time), all industries, both genders, ages 15 and over.
- **Reference period:** September 2026 compared with September 2025.
- **Calculation:** I computed the change from the two published values. It is not a published figure.

The series isn't seasonally adjusted, and it moves around from month to month. For example, it was $37.02 in August 2026 and $37.77 in April 2026. A same-month comparison across years is the safer way to read it.

In August 2026, Canada's job vacancy rate was **2.8%**, with **about 507,220 vacant positions**. These are seasonally adjusted figures. The rate was unchanged from July, and vacancies rose by about 5,200 from 502,030 in July.

Source: Statistics Canada, Table 14-10-0432-01 (seasonally adjusted, monthly), reference period August 2026.
- Job vacancies: vector v1481212145
- Job vacancy rate: vector v1481212147

I didn't pull the unadjusted figures (Table 14-10-0371-01), so they may differ slightly.

Canada's all-items CPI rose **3.1%** in the 12 months to September 2026.

- The index (2002=100) was 170.0 in September 2026 and 164.9 in September 2025. That gives 170.0 / 164.9 − 1 ≈ 3.1%. I calculated this from the rounded index values, so the figure could differ slightly from Statistics Canada's published rate.
- Source: Statistics Canada, Table 18-10-0004-01 (Consumer Price Index, monthly, not seasonally adjusted), Canada, all-items, vector v41690973. Link: https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=1810000401

Gasoline prices in Canada rose about **27.8%** in the 12 months to September 2026.

- The gasoline CPI index (2002=100) went from 209.4 in September 2025 to 267.6 in September 2026. That is a rise of 58.2 index points.
- The 27.8% figure is my own calculation from those two index values. I did not pull a published year-over-year rate.
- Source: Statistics Canada, Table 18-10-0004-01 (Consumer Price Index, monthly, not seasonally adjusted), Canada, Gasoline, vector v41691136. https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=1810000401

The index was lower than a year earlier for part of the period, falling to 188.6 in December 2025. It then climbed sharply from March 2026 and peaked at 273.7 in May 2026.

Prices for food purchased from stores in Canada rose **about 1.7%** in the 12 months to September 2026. This is my calculation from the index levels, not a published rate.

- The Consumer Price Index (CPI) for food purchased from stores was 198.3 in September 2026, up from 195.0 in September 2025. The base is 2002=100.
- 198.3 ÷ 195.0 = 1.0169, which rounds to 1.7%.
- The index peaked at 200.9 in May 2026 and has fallen since. It was 199.6 in August and 198.3 in September.

Source: Statistics Canada, Table 18-10-0004-01 (Consumer Price Index, monthly, not seasonally adjusted), Canada, "Food purchased from stores", vector v41690975. Reference periods: September 2025 and September 2026.

**Prince Edward Island** had the highest 12-month CPI inflation in September 2026, at about **5.7%**. I calculated this from the index levels, so it isn't a published rate.

- **PEI:** the all-items index rose from 168.1 (Sept 2025) to 177.6 (Sept 2026), which is +5.65%. Vector v41691379.
- **Nova Scotia** was a close second at about 5.6% (168.6 to 178.1). Vector v41691513.
- **Other provinces:** New Brunswick was 5.0%, Newfoundland and Labrador 4.7% and Manitoba 4.4%. Alberta was 3.6%, Saskatchewan 3.3%, Quebec 3.1%, British Columbia 3.0% and Ontario 2.5%.

PEI and Nova Scotia are only 0.1 percentage point apart. Rounding of the published one-decimal indexes could affect the ranking, so check StatCan's own published rates if the order matters.

Source: Statistics Canada, Table 18-10-0004-01 (Consumer Price Index, monthly, not seasonally adjusted), all-items, reference periods September 2025 and September 2026. https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=1810000401

CPI-common was **2.4%** year over year in September 2026. It was 2.6% in August, 2.7% in July and 2.6% in June.

Source: Statistics Canada, table 18-10-0256-01, "CPI-common (year-over-year percent change)", Canada, vector v108785713. Link: https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=1810025601

Canada's real GDP grew about **3.3% at an annualized rate** in Q2 2026 (April–June). That is my calculation from the published levels. I didn't find a published annualized rate in the tables I checked.

- **Quarterly growth:** real GDP rose 0.8% from Q1 to Q2 2026. Source: Statistics Canada table 36-10-0104-01, vector v1594571783, chained (2017) dollars, seasonally adjusted, percentage change.
- **Levels:** GDP at market prices went from $2,503,604 million in Q1 to $2,524,127 million in Q2. Source: the same table, vector v62305752, seasonally adjusted at annual rates.
- **Annualizing:** (2,524,127 / 2,503,604)⁴ − 1 ≈ 3.3%. Annualizing the rounded 0.8% gives about 3.2%, so the unrounded levels are the better basis.

Statistics Canada's own headline figure may differ slightly from mine because of rounding. Later revisions could also change it.

Canada's seasonally adjusted retail sales rose **about 1.2%** in August 2026 from July. That is an increase of about $883 million.

- July 2026: $73.68 billion
- August 2026: $74.57 billion

Source: Statistics Canada, Table 20-10-0056-01, "Monthly retail trade sales by province and territory". The series is Canada, total retail trade, total retail sales, seasonally adjusted (vector v1446859483). Reference periods are July and August 2026. The percentage is my own calculation from the published levels, not a figure StatCan published directly.

Canadian manufacturers' sales were about **$79.9 billion** in August 2026. That is up about **$1.16 billion, or 1.5%**, from $78.7 billion in July. These are seasonally adjusted figures.

- **August 2026:** $79,876,565 thousand
- **July 2026:** $78,718,193 thousand (revised, as published in the table)
- **June 2026:** $78,930,364 thousand, so July was a small dip of about 0.3% before August's gain.

Source: Statistics Canada, Table 16-10-0047-01, "Sales of goods manufactured (shipments)", Canada, total manufacturing, seasonally adjusted, vector v800450. Reference periods are July and August 2026. I calculated the dollar and percent changes myself from the published levels.

Canada's merchandise exports to the United States in August 2026 were **$54.46 billion** (customs basis, seasonally adjusted). That is up from $49.12 billion in July 2026, a rise of about 10.9%.

On an unadjusted basis, August exports were $52.19 billion. July's unadjusted figure was $49.49 billion.

Sources: Statistics Canada, Table 12-10-0011-01, International merchandise trade for all countries and by principal trading partners, monthly. Both series are in current dollars.
- Seasonally adjusted: vector v87008898.
- Unadjusted: vector v87008869.

Canada's seasonally adjusted annual rate of housing starts in September 2026 was **about 248,896 units**.

- That is up from 242,223 in August 2026, an increase of about 6,700 units. (The table shows 242.223 thousand for August.)
- Source: Statistics Canada, table 34-10-0158-01 (CMHC housing starts, all areas, seasonally adjusted at annual rates), vector v52300157, reference period September 2026.

Canada's building permits were worth **$13.57 billion** in August 2026 on a seasonally adjusted basis. This is the figure Statistics Canada normally headlines. It is up from $12.48 billion in July 2026, about 8.8% higher.

The unadjusted value was **$13.20 billion** for August 2026.

Both figures cover total residential and non-residential permits, all types of work, in current dollars.

Sources, both from Statistics Canada table 34-10-0292-01, Building permits, by type of structure and type of work (https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=3410029201):
- **Seasonally adjusted:** vector v1675119645, reference period 2026-08.
- **Unadjusted:** vector v1675115467, reference period 2026-08.

The table gives values in thousands of dollars. I took the vector numbers from the tool output, not from the published table page, so they are worth a quick check there.

British Columbia's population on July 1, 2026 was **5,710,598**.

- Source: Statistics Canada, Table 17-10-0009-01 (Population estimates, quarterly), reference period 2026-07 (July 1, 2026). The vector ID returned by the tool is v3. I haven't checked that against the published vector number.
- Context: the figure is up about 6,900 from April 1, 2026 (5,703,683). It is also up about 8,000 from July 1, 2025 (5,702,544).
- Quarterly estimates are often revised. Check the table link for the latest values: https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=1710000901
